market.headline: Futures are lower before the open: QQQ is at 684.02 after hours (-0.9%) and SPY at 756.1 (-0.5%). Two things are driving it: reports that Nvidia's board is preparing to oust Jensen Huang, and a hot October inflation report that has Fed officials talking about rate hikes. The Nvidia shock is today's main story.
watch: QQQ 683.56 (Wednesday's low): after hours it sits at 684.02, just above it. Above 683.56 after the first hour = the Nvidia hit stays contained. Below = Wednesday's rebound fails and the next stop is 667.05.

AMAT, CSCO and NBIS report today (dates estimated, times not confirmed). NBIS is CoreWeave's closest peer and AMAT supplies the chip makers. PPI is out Friday at 08:30, and another hot inflation number would add to rate-hike fears.
SPY 754.9 (Wednesday's low): above = the broad market is shrugging off Nvidia. Below = selling is spreading beyond tech.

stocks.headline: Down 8.6% after hours to 158.78, below its 52-week low of 163.9, on reports the board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang.
stocks.why: The selling is about the CEO and a US probe. The business itself is fine: sales are up 106%, the operating margin is 65%, and next year's profit forecasts are up 24% in 90 days. The stock trades at 11× next year's forecast. The real business risk is the probe into Megaspeed, the partner accused of sending restricted Nvidia chips to China. That probe can bring penalties and tighter export rules, and it is costing Nvidia goodwill in Washington. The company has no succession plan, and it reports around Nov 17, so the board's decision and the results can land in the same week. The selling spills over to suppliers and customers (MU, TSM, SMCI, CRWV, ORCL), while AMD and AVGO are being bought as the alternatives.

long_term.reason: Profits are growing faster than sales and the stock is at its cheapest in 5 years. The CEO drama does not change demand for its chips, but the export probe can cut into China sales.

stocks.what_would_change_it: Proof that Nvidia itself broke export rules, or a messy CEO exit with no clear successor, would make this Wait.
stocks.action: Don't buy the open. Buy a small first position only if it holds above 158.78 through the first hour, and add more only after the Nov 17 report.

levels.means: Above = it is back over its 52-week low and the panic is easing. Below = no floor yet.

Above = the whole drop is undone and the market is shrugging off the CEO news.

stocks.headline: Up 4.3% after hours to 576.76, after a 7.3% gain Wednesday, as money rotates out of Nvidia.
stocks.why: Investors are treating AMD as the safe way to own AI chips while Nvidia's leadership is in doubt. The business supports that: sales are up 45% and speeding up, the operating margin has doubled to 18%, it has beaten forecasts 5 quarters running, and next year's profit forecasts are up 15%. The risk is the price, not the business. At 31× next year's profit it costs far more than Nvidia, so if the Nvidia fear fades, this rotation can reverse fast. Expect big swings either way: the stock moves about twice as much as the index.

long_term.reason: Sales and profit forecasts are rising fast, but the stock is pricier than its peers, so buy pullbacks, not gaps.

stocks.what_would_change_it: A calm resolution at Nvidia that pulls buyers back there would make this Hold at these prices.
stocks.action: Don't chase the gap. Buy only on a pullback that holds above 567.65, or on a clean move through 579.18 after the first hour.

levels.means: Above = it breaks its 20-day high and the rotation has room to run. Below = it is still capped.

Below = the whole overnight gain is gone and the rotation failed, so stay out.

stocks.headline: Down 6.4% after hours to 56.9, giving back part of Wednesday's 24.7% post-earnings jump.
stocks.why: The results were good on top: sales are up 112%, it beat on revenue, raised its forecast, and the CEO canceled his planned share sale. The problem is underneath. It is still losing money (-1.27 per share last quarter, a -3% operating margin), carries $24.9B of long-term debt against $5.5B of cash, and now asks customers to prepay and borrows against single contracts to fund growth. That model works only while credit is cheap and Nvidia chips flow freely. Talk of Fed hikes threatens the first, and the Nvidia probe threatens the second. NBIS reports today, and weak numbers there would hit this stock next.

long_term.reason: The $103.7B backlog is real, but losses and heavy debt make the stock depend on credit markets that are getting tighter.

stocks.what_would_change_it: A quarter with a positive operating margin and less reliance on new borrowing would make this a Wait.
stocks.action: Don't buy. If you hold it, sell into any bounce toward 60.77 today.

levels.means: Above = buyers are still backing the earnings story. Below = the post-earnings pop is fading.
